title: Digital Lending and Buy Now, Pay Later
summary: How algorithmic lenders and BNPL providers originate, fund and collect credit, where affordability and credit risk are mispriced, and what supervisors test in their models and outcomes.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How algorithmic lenders and BNPL providers originate, fund and collect credit, where affordability and credit risk are mispriced, and what supervisors test in their models and outcomes.
Learning Objectives: Explain the origination, funding and collections models of digital lenders
Assess affordability testing, credit models and arrears management
Identify red flags in BNPL growth, merchant incentives and repeat borrowing
Syllabus: Alternative data, automated credit decisions and model drift
Funding through warehouse lines, forward flow and securitisation
BNPL economics: merchant fees, late fees and stacked borrowing
Intended Audience: Supervisors, authorisation and innovation-hub staff dealing with FinTech applicants and fast-growing digital firms
Policy, consumer protection and financial crime specialists assessing new business models
Compliance, risk and legal teams in FinTech firms who want to see their firm the way a supervisor does
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of supervision, authorisation or compliance in financial services is helpful. No technical or financial modelling background is required.
Core Reading: FATF, Opportunities and Challenges of New Technologies for AML/CFT (2021)
G20/OECD High-Level Principles on Financial Consumer Protection (2022)
FSB, The Use of Supervisory and Regulatory Technology by Authorities and Regulated Institutions (2020)
